senses.gloss:
चत् चत्, cl. 1. P. A. चतति, -ते, occurring
only in pres. part. and past. and fut. pass.
part. (see below), Ved. to hide one's self; to go; to
ask, beg, solicit [cf. चद्]: Caus. P. A. चातयति, -ते,
-यितुम्, to cause to hide; to scare, frighten away;
[cf. Gr. χατέω, χατίζω.]

चतत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, hiding one's self; (Sāy.)
going, residing in, being in.

चतित, or Ved. चत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, hidden, made
to disappear.

चतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. hiding one's self; (Sāy.)
destroying enemies, frightening away.

चत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be hidden^1 &c.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210422. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/60.
चातक, अस्, m. See s. v.

चातक चातक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. चत्),
N. of the bird Cuculus Melanoleucus, according to
the legend living only upon rain-drops; [cf. Lat.
cot-urnix.]
—चातकानन्दन (˚क-आन्˚), अस्, m.
the rainy season.
—चातकाष्टक (˚क-अष्˚), अम्,
n. the eight verses on the Cātaka bird.

चातन, अस्, आ, अम्, driving away, removing [cf.
अभिशस्ति-च्˚, अमीव-च्˚, अराय-च्˚]; (अम्), n., scil.
सूक्तम्, certain verses of the Atharva-veda, the object
of which is to avert evil demons; (अस्), m., N. of
the supposed Ṛṣi of these verses of the Atharva-
veda.
चातन चातन. See under rt. चत् at p. 313.

चतुर् चतुर्, चत्वारस् m. pl.,
चत्वारि n. pl. (said to be fr. rt. चत्), four. In Vedic
Sanskrit the inst., dat., abl., and loc. have the accent
on the penultimate; in the later language either on
the penultimate or on the last syllable. A Vedic form
of the gen. pl. fem. चतसॄणाम् for चतसृणाम्
occurs sometimes in Epic poetry; [cf. Gr. τέσσαρες,
τέτταρες; Æol. πίσυρες; Goth. fidvor; Cambro-
Brit. pedwar, pedair; Lat. quatuor; Lith. keturi;
Slav. cetyrje; Hib. ceathair, ceteora; Zend cathru.]

पञ्चन्.
—चतुःपञ्चाश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 54th.

अधिक-शत, अस्, ई, अम्, the 154th.

पत्त्री, f., N. of a plant, = क्षुद्र-पाषाण-भेदी.
—चतुः-पर्णी, f. a kind of sorrel (क्षुद्राम्लिका).
—चतुः-पार्श्व, अम्, n. the four sides of a square.
—चतुः-पुण्ड्र, अस्, m., N. of a shrub, = भिण्डा.

बला).

—चतुः-
शत-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 104th.
—चतुः-शाल, अस्,
[]
आ, अम्, having four halls; built in a square; (अम्,
आ), n. f. or चतुः-शालक, अम्, n. a square of four
houses; a quadrangle enclosed by four buildings.
—च-
तुः-शृङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, four-horned; (अस्), m., N.

—चतुः-श्रोत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having
four ears.
—चतुःषष्ट, अस्, ई, अम्, the 64th;
having 64 added.

ई, अम्, the 64th.

with Sana (सनक, सनन्द, सनातन, सनत्कु-

—चतुः-सप्तति, इस्, f., 74.
—चतुःसप्तति-तम,
अस्, ई, अम्, the 74th.
—चतुः-सम, अम्, n. an
unguent of four ingredients, sandal, agallochum,
saffron, and musk; (अस्, आ, अम्), one whose body
has four smooth places.
—चतुः-सहस्र, अम्, n.,
1004; 4000.
—चतुः-सीमा, f. a border or boun-
dary on all four sides.
—चतुः-स्रक्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved.
quadrangular.
—चतुर्-अंश, अस्, m. a fourth part.
—चतुर्-अक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having four eyes.
—चतुर्-अक्षर, अम्, n. an aggregate or com-
bination of four syllables; (अस्, आ, अम्), consisting of
four syllables.
—चतुर्-अङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting
of four members, quadripartite; (चतुर्-अङ्गम्

सेना, an entire army &c.; (अम्), n. an entire army

—चतुरङ्ग-बल, अम्, n. an
entire army &c.; [cf. the preceding.]
—चतुरङ्ग-
बलाध्यक्ष (˚ल-अध्˚), अस्, m. the commander-
in-chief of a complete army.
—चतुरङ्ग-सैन्य,
अम्, n. an entire army; [cf. चतुर्-अङ्ग.]
—चतुर्-
अङ्गिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having four parts or members,
quadripartite; (इणी), f. a complete army.
—चतुर्-
अङ्गुल, अम्, n. the four fingers of the hand (with-

(अस्), m. the plant Cathartocarpus Fistula.
—चतुर्-
अध्यायिका, अम्, f. n. a collection of four Adhyāyas.

—चतुर्-अनुगान, अम्, n., N.
of a Sāman.

four sides; (आ), f. the earth.
—चतुरन्तेश (˚ता-ईश),
अस्, m. lord of the earth, a king.
—चतुर्-अवत्त,
अस्, आ, अम् (see अव-दो), divided into four parts;
(अम्), n. division into four parts.
—चतुर्-अवत्तिन्,
ई, इनी, इ (see अव-दो), one who is accustomed to
offer the havis in four portions.
—चतुरशीत, अस्,
ई, अम्, the 84th.
—चतुर्-अशीति, इस्, f., 84.
—चतुर्-
अशीति-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 84th.
—चतुर्-अश्र or

—चतुर्-अस्रक, अस्, m., N. of various postures in

—चतुर्-अह, अम्, n. a period

—चतुर्-आत्मन्, आ, आ, अ, re-
presenting four persons; having four faces.
—चतुर्-
आनन, अस्, आ, अम्, having four faces; (अस्), m. an
epithet of Brahmā.
—चतुर्-आनर्तन, अम्, n. a
dance by four, or in four divisions.

पद-स्तोभ, अम्, n., N. of a Sāman.
—चतुर्-
उत्तर, अस्, आ, अम्, increasing by four.
—चतुर्-
उषण, अम्, n. the four hot spices, black pepper,
long pepper, dry ginger, and the root of long pepper;
[cf. त्र्य्-ऊषण and चतुर्-जातक.]
—चतुर्-गति,
इस्, m. a tortoise (going on four feet).
—चतुर्-गर,
अम्, n. a carriage drawn by four oxen.
—चतुर्-
गुण, अस्, आ, अम्, four times, four-fold, quadruple.
—चतुर्-गृहीत, अस्, आ, अम्, taken up (or ladled
out, as a fluid) four times; (अम्), n. taking up (any
fluid) four times.
—चतुर्-ग्राम, अस् or अम् (?),
m. or n. (?), N. of a country.
—चतुर्-जातक, अम्,

तुर्णवत, अस्, ई, अम्, with 94 added (e. g. चतुर्-
णवतं शतम् = 194); [cf. चतुर्-नवत.]
[]
—चतुर्-दंष्ट्र, अस्, m. ‘having four tusks;’ N. of
Viṣṇu; of one of the attendants of Skanda; of a
Dānava.
—चतुर्-दत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, four-toothed.
—चतुर्-दन्त, अस्, m. ‘having four tusks,’ an epi-
thet of Airāvata, the elephant of Indra; N. of an ele-
phant mentioned in the Pañca-tantra.
—चतुर्दश,
अस्, ई, अम्, the fourteenth; consisting of fourteen; (ई),
f., scil. रात्रि, the fourteenth day in a lunar fortnight.
—चतुर्दश-धा, ind. fourteen-fold.
—चतुर्-
दशन्, अ, pl. fourteen; [cf. Lat. quatuordecim;
Lith. keturôlika.]
—चतुर्दशम, अस्, ई, अम्, the
fourteenth.
—चतुर्दश-मत-विवेक, अस्, m. title
of a work by Śaṅkara.
—चतुर्दशिक, अस् or अम्,
m. or n. (?), a feast on the fourteenth day of a lunar
fortnight.
—चतुर्-दारिक, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?),
N. of the fifth Lambaka in the Kathā-sarit-sāgara.
—चतुर्-दिक्षु or चतुर्-दिशम्, ind. towards the
four quarters, on all sides, all around.
—चतुर्-दोल,
अस्, अम्, m. n. a royal litter.
—चतुर्-द्वीप-चक्र-
वर्तिन्, ई, m. the sovereign of the four Dvīpas.
—चतुर्-धा, ind. in four parts, four-fold; [cf. Hib.
ceathardha; Gr. τέτραχα.]
—चतुर्धा-भू, cl. 1.
P. -भवति, -वितुम्, to be divided into four parts.
—चतुर्धा-शान्ति, इस्, f. a religious ceremony per-
formed at the time of making the stated offerings to
deceased ancestors.
—चतुर्नवत, अस्, ई, अम्, the
94th.
—चतुर्-नवति, इस्, f., 94.
—चतुर्नवति-
तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 94th.
—चतुर्-बाहु, उस्, उस्, उ,
four-armed; an epithet of Viṣṇu and Śiva; [cf. च-
तुर्-भुज.]
—चतुर्-भद्र, अम्, n. the aggregate of
four objects of human wishes, viz. धर्म, virtue;
काम, pleasure; अर्थ, wealth; and मोक्ष, final
beatitude.
—चतुर्-भाग, अस्, m. the fourth part, a
quarter.
—चतुर्-भुज, अम्, n. (generally in com-
pounds), four arms; (अस्, आ, अम्), having four arms;
quadrangular; (अस्), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu or
Kṛṣṇa; a square; N. of a Dānava; N. of the
instructor of Rāmānanda; N. of the father of Śiva-
datta.
—चतुर्भुज-भट्टाचार्य (˚ट-आच्˚), अस्, m.,
N. of an author.
—चतुर्-भूगस्, आन्, असी, अस्, con-
taining four (syllables) more.
—चतुर्-महाराज, आस्,
m. pl. the four great kings or gods of the highest of
the six Buddhist heavens.
—चतुर्महाराज-कायिक,
अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the group of the four great
kings; epithet of a class of deities with Buddhists;
also चतुर्महाराजिक.
—चतुर्-मास, अम्, n. a
period of four months.
—चतुर्-मुख, अम्, n. (in
compounds), four faces; (अस्, ई, अम्), having four

epithet of Brahmā, of Viṣṇu, Śiva, and of a Dānava;
a preparation of mercury (?).
—चतुर्मुख-रस,
अस्, m. a preparation of great curative power.
—च-
तुर्-युग, अम्, n. the aggregate of the four Yugas
or ages of the world, a Mahā-yuga or 4,320,000
years; (अस्, आ, अम्), drawn by four (oxen &c.);

—चतर्-युज्. क्, क्, क्, drawn by four (oxen &c.).
—चतुर्-वक्त्र, अस्, m. ‘four-faced,’ N. of Brahmā;

—चतुर्-वय, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. four-fold.
—चतुर्-वर्ग, अस्, m. a collection of four things,

—चतुर्वर्ग-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m.
title of a work.
—चतुर्-वर्ण, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?),
the four classes or castes of Hindūs, viz. Brāhmans,
Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras; four principal
colours; four letters.
—चतुर्वर्ण-मय, अस्, ई,
अम्, consisting of the four castes.
—चतुर्वर्ण्य,
अम्, n. the system of the four castes.
—चतुर्-वर्-
षिका, f., scil. गो, a cow four years old.
—चतुर्-
वाहिन्, ई, m., scil. रथ, a carriage drawn by four
(horses &c.).
—चतुर्विंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 24th;
having 24 added (e. g. चतुर्विंशं शतम्, 124);
consisting of 24; (अस्), m., N. of a Stoma; (अम्), n.,
scil. अहन्, N. of an Ekāha.
—चतुर्-विंशति, इस्, f.,
24; the 24th year (e. g. आ-चतुर्विंशं शतम्, to the
24th year); title of a work.
—चतुर्विंशतिक,
अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of 24.
—चतुर्विंशति-तम,
अस्, ई, अम्, the 24th.
—चतुर्विंशति-मत, अम्, n.
‘24 sects,’ title of a work.
—चतुर्विंशतिमत-
व्याख्या, f. a commentary by Bhaṭṭoji-dīkṣita.
—चतुर्विंशत्य्-अवतार-चरित्र, अम्, n. ‘history
[]
of 24 incarnations’ by Narahara-dāsa.
—चतुर्विंशा-
क्षर, अस्, आ, अम्, containing 24 syllables.
—चतुर्-
विद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, familiar with the four Vedas; (अस्),
m. one who has studied the four Vedas.
—चतुर्-
विध, अस्, आ, अम्, four-fold; of four sorts or kinds,
in four ways.
—चतुर्-वीज, अम्, n. the four kinds of
seed, i. e. the seed of Kālājājī, Candra-śūra, Me-
thikā, and Yavānikā.
—चतुर्-वीर, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. an epithet applied to a particular unguent; also
to a Soma sacrifice which lasts four days.
—चतुर्-
वेद, आस्, m. pl., the four Vedas, viz. the Ṛg-veda,
Yajur-veda, Sāma-veda, and Atharva-veda; (अस्, आ,
अम्), containing the four Vedas; familiar with the

—चतुर्-
वेदिन्, ई, इणी, इ, familiar with the four Vedas.
—चतुर्-व्यूह, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu; [cf.

—चतुर्-हनु, उस्, m. ‘having four
jaws,’ N. of a Dānava.
—चतुर्-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्,
four-armed.
—चतुर्-हायण, अस्, ई, अम्, four years
old; (ई), f. a cow of four years.
—चतुर्-होतृ, ता
or तारस्, m. sing. or plur., N. of a certain liturgical
section of Vedic works intended for recitation; con-
taining the four chief priests.
—चतुर्-होत्र, अस्, m.
comprehending the four chief priests.
—चतुर्हो-
त्रक, अम्, n. the four chief priests; the duties of
these priests.
—चतुश्चत्वारिंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 44th;
having 44 added; containing 44; (अस्), m., N. of a
Stoma.
—चतुश्-चत्वारिंशत्, त्, f., 44.
—चतुष्-
कर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, four-eared; heard by four ears

Skanda.
—चतुष्कर्ण-ता, f. the state of being
heard by only four ears, a secret.
—चतुष्-कोण, अस्,
आ, अम्, square, quadrangular; (अस्), m. a quadrangular
figure, a square, a tetragon.
—चतु-ष्टोम, अस्, m.
(fr. चतुर् and स्तोम), a Stoma consisting of four
parts; (अस्, आ, अम्), connected with such a Stoma.
—चतुष्-पथ, अस्, अम्, m. n. a place where four
roads meet, a cross-way; (अस्), m. a Brāhman (so
called from the four आश्रमास्, q. v.).
—चतुष्पथ-
निकेता or चतुष्पथ-रता, f., N. of one of the
Mātṛs attendant on Skanda.
—चतुष्-पद, अस्,
आ, अम्, having four feet; consisting of four Pādas;
(in arithmetic or algebra) tetranomial; (अस्), m. an
animal with four legs, a quadruped; (in astron.) a
term for certain signs of the zodiac; N. of a par-

(अम्), n. a conjunction of four Pādas.
—चतुष्प-
दिका, f., N. of a metre containing 30 + 4 + 4 syllabic
instants.
—चतुष्-पाटी, f. a river (winding four
ways ?).
—चतुष्-पाठी, f. a school for Brāhmans

—चतुष्-पाणि,
इस्, इस्, इ, four-handed; (इस्), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu.

divided into four parts, consisting of four parts;

four processes, plea, defence, rejoinder, and sentence;
(-पदी), f. a female quadruped; (-पत्), n. the quadru-
peds collectively, the animals.
—चतुष्-पाद, अस्,
ई, अम्, quadruped; divided into four parts, consisting
of four parts; (अस्), m. a quadruped.
—चतुष्-
पार्श्व, अम्, n. the four sides of anything.
—चतु-
स्तन, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. चतुः-स्तन), having four
nipples.
—चतुस्त्रिंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 34th; having
34 added; containing 34.
—चतुस्त्रिंशज्-जातक-
ज्ञ, अस्, m. a Buddha.
—चतुस्-त्रिंशत्, त्, f., 34.
—चतुस्-सम, see चतुः-सम.
—चतू-राजी, f.
(fr. चतुर् + राजन्), the four kings; N. of the
luckiest or most desired termination of the game
called Caturaṅga, by which one king gains the four
thrones.
—चतू-रात्र, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. चतुर् + रात्र),
lasting four days (lit. nights); (अस् or अम्), m. n., N.
of a certain ceremony.

1. चतुर, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of some com-
pounds) = चतुर्, four; see अ-च्˚, उप-च्˚, त्रि-च्˚.
(For 2. चतुर see next col.)

चतुर 2. चतुर, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr.
rt. चत्; for 1. see under चतुर् above), swift, quick;
dexterous, clever, skilful, ingenious; charming, agree-
able; visible, perceptible; (अस्), m. a round pillow,
one for the cheek; (अम्), n. skilfulness, cleverness;
an elephant's stable; [cf. चातुर.]
—चतुर-ता, f.
cleverness, skilfulness, cunningness.

चातुर 1. चातुर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्), re-
lating to four; (a carriage &c.) drawn by four; (ई),
f., N. of a poem by Nara-siṃha; (अम्), n. a carriage,
a cart holding four people.

चातुर 2. चातुर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. चतुर),
clever, able, ingenious, shrewd, sagacious; speaking
well or kindly, flattering; perceptible, visible; govern-
ing, ruling; (अस्), m. a small round pillow, see below;
(ई), f. dexterity, ability, cleverness.

चतुर्थ, अस्, ई, अम्, fourth, the fourth; (अस्), m.
the fourth letter in every class of consonants, i. e. घ्,
झ्, ढ्, ध्, भ्; (ई), f., scil. रात्रि, the fourth day
[]
in a lunar fortnight; (scil. विभक्ति), the termination
of the fourth case, the fourth case, the dative case;
(अस्, आ, अम्), constituting the fourth part; (अम्), n.
a quarter; [cf. Lith. ketwirtas; Slav. cetvertyi,
cetvertaja; Gr. τέταρος; Lat. quartus; Goth.
fidvorda (?); Germ. vierter.]
—चतुर्थ-कर्मन्,
अ, n. the ceremonies performed on the fourth day of
a marriage.
—चतुर्थ-कालम्, ind. at the fourth
meal, at the evening of every second day of a person's
fasting.
—चतुर्थकालिक, अस्, आ, अम्, one who passes
three meals without eating and partakes only of the
fourth.
—चतुर्थ-फल, अम्, n. the second in-
equality or equation of a planet.
—चतुर्थ-भक्त,
अम्, n. consuming the fourth meal (after having passed
three without eating).
—चतुर्थ-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, re-
ceiving the fourth part as a toll from one's subjects (as
a king).
—चतुर्थ-स्वर, अम्, n., N. of a Sāman.
—चतुर्थांश (˚थ-अं˚), अस्, m. a quarter, a
fourth part; (अस्, आ, अम्), receiving a quarter.
—च-
तुर्थाश्रम (˚थ-आश्˚), अस्, m. the fourth order
of a Brāhman's life.
चतुर्थ चतुर्थ. See col. 2.

चतुर्थक, अस्, आ, अम्, the fourth; returning or
repeated every four days as a fever, quartan; (इका),
f. a weight equal to four Karṣas or one Pāla.

चातुर्थक, अस्, इका, अम्, quartan, appearing
every fourth day; (अस्), m. a quartan ague.
चतुर्य, nom. P. चतुर्यति, to wish for four.

चातुर्य, अम्, n. dexterity, cleverness, ability,
shrewdness; amiableness.

चतुष्क, अस्, आ, अम्, four, consisting of four,
increased by four (e. g. चतुष्कं शतम् = 104
or four per cent; (अस्), m., N. of a man; (ई), f. a
large four-sided pond or tank; a bed or musquito-
curtain; (अम्), n. the number four; a collection of
four; a cross-way; a quadrangular court-yard [cf.
चत्वर]; a hall resting on four columns; a neck-
lace of four strings.
चतुष्किका, f. the number four.

चतुष्किन्, ई, इणी, इ, having four (parts &c.) of
anything.

चतुष्टय, अस्, ई, अम्, four-fold, consisting of
four; (अम्), n. the number four, a collection of four,
an aggregate of four, a quaternion; a square; a
collection of Sūtras consisting of four sections; the
first, fourth, seventh, and tenth signs of the zodiac;
the centre of a circle.
—चतुष्टय-समास, आस्,
m. pl. four classes of compounds, viz. Avyayī-bhāva,
Tat-puruṣa, Dvandva, and Bahu-vrīhi.

चातुष्टय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुष्टय), knowing
or familiar with the Catuṣṭaya.
चतुस्, ind. four times; [cf. Zend cathrus.]

चत्वर, अम्, n. a quadrangular place or court-
yard, a place in which many ways meet; a levelled
spot of ground prepared for a sacrifice.
—चत्वर-
वासिनी, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs attendant on
Skanda.

चत्वारिंश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the next), the 40th;
having 40 added; consisting of 40.

चात्वारिंश, अम्, n. (fr. चत्वारिंशत्), title of a
Brāhmaṇa consisting of forty Adhyāyas.
चत्वारिंशत् चत्वारिंशत्. See above.

चत्वारिंशति, इस्, f. = the preceding (in द्वा-चत्वा-
रिंशति).

चतुरक, अस्, m., N. of a jackal; (इका), f., N.
of a woman.

चतुल चतुल, अस्, आ, अम्, depositing, placing,
fixing.

चत्वाल चत्वाल, अस्, m. a hole in the ground
&c. prepared for an oblation with fire, or for the sacri-
ficial fire; the womb; Kuśa grass; [cf. चात्वाल.]

चात्वाल चात्वाल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. the hole
formed in the ground by excavating the earth to con-
struct the Uttara-vedi or north altar; (अस्), m. a
hollow place dug in the ground to receive a burnt-offer-
ing; any hole in the ground; [cf. चत्वाल.]
—चा-
त्वाल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, (a sacrifice) at which the
Cātvāla is excavated.

चातुःसागरिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुः-सागर),
belonging to the four oceans.

चातुरक्ष, अम्, n. (fr. चतुर्-अक्ष), four casts
in playing at dice.

चातुरर्थिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-अर्थ), used
in four particular senses or meanings.

चातुराश्रमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, or चातुराश्रमिन्,
ई, इणी, इ (fr. चतुर्-आश्रम), being in one of the
four periods or orders [cf. आश्रम] of life.

चातुराश्रम्य, अम्, n. the four periods of the
life of a Brāhman collectively; the aggregate of the
four orders of student, householder, ascetic, and
mendicant.
चातुर्जातक, अम्, n. = कटु-चातुर्जातक.

चातुर्थाह्निक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्थ-अहन्),
belonging to the fourth day.

चातुर्थिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the fourth
or to the fourth day; (अस्), m. a quartan ague.

चातुर्दश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्दशी), appearing
on the fourteenth day of the half month.

चातुर्दशिक, अस्, ई, अम्, reading the holy scrip-
tures on the fourteenth day of the half month.

चातुर्दैव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-देव), sacred to
four deities.

चातुर्भद्र, अम्, n. (fr. चतुर्-भद्र), an
assemblage of four medicinal plants.
चातुर्भुजि, इस्, m. a son of Catur-bhuja.

चातुर्भौतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-भूत),
consisting of four elements.

चातुर्महाराजकायिक or चातुर्महाराजिक =
चतुर्महाराजकायिक; also an epithet of Viṣṇu.

चातुर्मास, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-मास), produced
in four months.

चातुर्मासक, अस्, इका, अम्, or चातुर्मासिन्, ई,
इनी, इ, one who performs the Cāturmāsya sacrifice.

चातुर्मासी, f., scil. पौर्णमासी, the day of full
moon at the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

चातुर्मास्य, अम्, n., N. of three sacrifices be-
longing to the subdivision called Havir-yajña and
performed (every four months) at the beginning of
the three seasons, viz. the वैश्वदेवम् on the full
moon in Phalguna, वरुण-प्रघासाः in Aṣāḍha,
and साकमेधाः in Kṛttikā; (अस्, आ, अम्), belong-
ing to the Cāturmāsya sacrifice.

चातुर्वर्ण्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. चतुर्-वर्ण), suited
to the four tribes or castes, belonging to them (?);
(अम्), n. the aggregate of the four original castes,
viz. the Brāhman, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra.

चातुर्विंशिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्विंश), be-
longing to the twenty-fourth day.

चातुर्विद्य, अस्, दी, अम् (fr. चतुर्-विद्या), familiar
with the four Vedas; (अम्), n. the four Vedas.

चातुर्विध्य, अम्, n. (fr. चतुर्-विध), four kinds
collectively.

चातुर्वैद्य, अस्, दी, अम् (fr. चतुर्-वेद), versed
in or familiar with the four Vedas; (अम्), n. know-
ledge of the four Vedas.

चातुर्होतृक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-होतृ), belong-
ing to the Catur-hotṛ.

चातुर्होत्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-होतृ), conducted
[]
or performed by the four chief priests, viz. the Hotṛ,
Adhvaryu, Udgātṛ, and Brahman; (अम्), n. a sacrifice
performed by four priests; the office or duties of the
four chief priests; the four chief priests collectively.

चातुर्होत्रिय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुर्-होतृ), a sacri-
fice &c. at or in which the four chief priests are
employed.

चातुष्काण्डिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. चतुष्-काण्ड),
divided into four parts.

चातुष्प्राश्य, अस्, शी, अम् (fr. चतुः + प्राश),
enough for four persons to eat.
चात्वारिंशत्क, अस्, ई, अम्, bought for forty.
चातुरिक, अस्, m. a charioteer, a coachman.

चात्र चात्र, अम्, n. (sometimes read चत्र),
a cylinder of catechu-wood twelve Aṅgulas long,
tipped at both ends with iron and furnished with an
iron bolt, (this and another piece of wood called
Auvīlī are used for producing the sacred fire.)
